Subject: 3yr prepay options + ramp plan (procurement questions attached)

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to pull together the finance side: we are seriously evaluating a 3-year prepay to get predictability (and a better unit price), but we need a structure that handles our seasonal ramp and annual true-ups.

Attached is a short questionnaire (procurement_questions.xlsx) with our expected usage profile by quarter and a few compliance questions. High level: our forecast for year 1 is ~35% of the total committed tokens, year 2 ~40%, year 3 ~25% (growth concentrated in Q2/Q3).

Can Redwood provide:
- A worked example for a 3-year prepaid discount vs annual prepay (with quarterly true-ups)?
- A staged/ramp-friendly pricing option (so we don’t overcommit early and be locked into wasted prepay)?
- Any guardrails or caps on credits for under-usage?

We’re targeting a procurement review on Tue 5/18 — would like a proposal before then.

Thanks,
Claire Jennings
Senior Procurement Manager
NorthBridge Health

On Mon, May 10, 2026 at 09:12 AM Claire Jennings <claire.jennings@northbridgehealth.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the demo...

Claire — appreciate the details and the upload. I’ve sketched two practical structures that typically work for customers with seasonal adoption:

1) "Flat prepay" (3yr upfront): single upfront payment, steeper discount (best unit price), annual true-up only. Good if you want simplest accounting.

2) "Staggered prepay + quarterly true-up" (recommended for your profile): commit to a 3yr total but allow a staged drawdown / quarterly true-ups that refund/credit substantial under-usage. Effective discount is slightly lower than flat prepay, but minimizes overpayment risk during year-1 ramp. Example attached (NBH_MA_proposal_v1.pdf).

Quick ask from my side: can you confirm the quarterly split expectation (you gave 35/40/25 for years, but we need quarter-level for year 1 to size the staged tranche)? If you want, I can propose a 40/35/25 year-level ramp with quarterly measurement and a true-up that pays credits back up to a 12% cap of the initial payment (prelim).

I’ve cc’ed Ben (sales lead) to loop him in on commercial flexibility. We can get a version for procurement by 5/14 if you confirm quarter-level usage or allow us to use the attached forecast.

Regards,

Subject: Internal: NBH - request for 3yr staggered prepay approval (numbers inside)

Team — looping you in. NorthBridge is asking for a 3-year prepaid structure with ramp protection; high-level ask below. I need a final commercial position and approval to include the terms in the proposal.

Summary:
- ARR profile (customer forecast): Year1 ~ $1.2M equivalent usage, Year2 ~$1.4M, Year3 ~$0.9M (aggregate committed tokens ~ $3.5M over 3 years)
- Proposed structures to offer: (A) 3yr upfront at 22% list discount (best price) or (B) staggered prepay with quarterly true-up at 18% list discount + staged tranche release (40% upfront, 35% at start of year2, 25% at start of year3).
- Risk controls requested by procurement: quarterly true-ups, cap credits at ~12% of initial prepay, and an annual minimum usage floor to avoid churn.

Why staggered option: fits their ramp, retains revenue visibility, lowers refund exposure in Y1.

I recommend option (B) as the go-to proposal to get them across the line while protecting Redwood. Need finance approval on the effective discount and the credit cap wording. If we can do 18% with the described cap, procurement will likely sign. If finance will not accept, we can push 20% as an alternative.

Please advise — Laura, any redlines on the credit cap / SOW/payment terms we should preempt? Ben/Karthik — any pricing levers (credits vs committed minimums) you want me to bake into version 2?

Thanks,
Mateo

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: NBH - request for 3yr staggered prepay approval (numbers inside)

Mateo / team — I reviewed the ask and the numbers. We can approve a staggered 3-year prepay, with the following conditions: 

1) Approved discount: 18% off list for the staggered structure (effective discount for the customer).
2) Credit/true-up cap: credits for under-usage capped at 10% of the total initial prepay amount (lower than ask; this reduces credit exposure).
3) Minimum annual usage floor: require a 70% annualized usage floor per year or the customer pays the difference as a settlement in the following quarter.
4) Payment terms: 30 days for tranche 1; tranche 2 and 3 invoiced at the start of year2/year3 with 30 days net. We will not accept deferred payment beyond 45 days without senior approval.
4) Contractual protections: include a clawback clause limited to usage-based credits only; no SLA credits to be applied against prepay.

If NorthBridge insists on a deeper discount (>=20%), escalate to Sales Ops + VP-Sales for exception. Otherwise, proceed with option B (18% + 10% credit cap + 70% floor).

I will prepare the finance-approved clause language for the SOW. Please include the HubSpot deal id NBH-2026-07 in the proposal.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

Good news: Finance has approved a staggered 3-year prepay structure for NorthBridge with the following committed commercial terms (summary):
- Total 3yr commitment: $3,500,000 (example numbers per your forecast)
- Discount: 18% off list for the staggered structure
- Tranche schedule: 40% paid at signature (tranche 1), 35% invoiced at start of year2, 25% invoiced at start of year3

- Minimum usage floor: 70% annualized floor per year; shortfall settles in the following quarter
- Payment terms: net 30 for each tranche; DocuSign SOW to include specific payment schedule and clawback language
